correctness.rationale: The weighted signed cofactor is the unnormalized tree character sum by the polynomial matrix-tree identity, and on the constants' orthogonal complement its Laplacian is nI-2L_S. The resulting product divided by n holds also when extra zero eigenvalues occur. For k positive, each nontrivial component has v<=k+1 and Laplacian norm at most v by the complementary Laplacian identity. Equality k+1 requires a component with all k edges, v=k+1, hence a tree with disconnected complement. The complement components force all cross edges in the tree, and a cut with both sides of size at least two would make a four-cycle; the tree is therefore a star. Conversely a star reaches the bound. This independently gives exactly the subcritical positivity and the equality case; the empty support is positive by Cayley. On k-edge stars the remaining nonzero spectrum is k-1 copies of 1, which gives the stated product and the strict negative witness at k=m. Modulo two every tree contributes 1, giving odd nonzero coefficients at odd n, and the unnormalized characters diagonalize the operator. The case n=4 counts six edges without doubling; higher first-zero stars have unique centers. Independently written audit-checks/cayley.py checks all supports through the boundary at n=4,6,8,10 via incidence-Gram determinants, giving 6,60,280,1260 zeros and the claimed negative-star coefficients at n=4,6,8; these are corroboration, not the general proof.
residual_risks: No classification of higher-degree zeros or even-order total rank is established or claimed.
